title: Bitmessage: A Peer-to-Peer Message Authentication and Delivery System
note: Original design: addresses as hash of two public keys, streams to partition load, 2-day TTL, PoW sized by message length and TTL, ECIES encryption without forward secrecy.
bitmessage_link: The subject: every message is flooded to every node of a stream, encrypted to the recipient public key, admitted by a hashcash-style proof of work; recipients trial-decrypt everything; broadcasts use a key derived from the sender address.

title: Bitmessage Protocol specification (wiki, protocol v3)
note: Page text saved as Markdown; text says protocol v3 is mandatory from 2014-11-16. Living document, year is first protocol version.
bitmessage_link: The normative wire protocol: version/inv/getdata/object messages, object types getpubkey, pubkey, msg, broadcast, inventory vectors and the double-SHA-512 proof of work.

title: PyBitmessage repository protocol documentation (address, encryption, proof of work, extended encoding, protocol)
authors: Bitmessage developers (PyBitmessage docs/ directory, branch v0.6)
note: Concatenation of docs/address.rst, encryption.rst, encrypted_payload.rst, pow.rst, pow_formula.rst, extended_encoding.rst, protocol.rst fetched from the v0.6 branch.
bitmessage_link: Defines address derivation, ECIES (secp256k1 ECDH, AES-256-CBC, HMAC-SHA256), the proof-of-work target formula with TTL and extra bytes, and extended message encoding; the static-key encryption and PoW admission that later work criticises.

title: Bitmessage Wiki FAQ
note: Operational description of chans (mailing-list style shared keys), Tor use and the PoW wait; used to ground the chan and stream claims.
bitmessage_link: Explains chans (shared passphrase as address), streams, the 2-day retention, the cost of sending and why every node receives every message.

title: PyBitmessage Changelog (wiki)
note: Useful for dating protocol v3, the extended-encoding change that led to CVE-2018-1000070, and Tor-related fixes.
bitmessage_link: Release-by-release record of protocol changes (PoW parameters, TTL, streams, Tor and I2P handling, the 0.6.3.2 fix) that shows how the design drifted from the whitepaper.

title: Bitmessage Wiki main page: remote code execution notice for PyBitmessage 0.6.2
note: States that the exploit was seen in use, the fix is 0.6.3.2 and 0.6.1 is unaffected; also states the project had no security audit.
bitmessage_link: Vendor notice that a malformed object processed by 0.6.2 could execute code on any receiving node, which is the cost of processing every message from every sender.

title: CVE-2018-1000070 and CVE-2021-26917: PyBitmessage vulnerability records (NVD)
note: CVSS 3.0 8.8 for the first record, fixed in 0.6.3 (commit 3a8016d). Record text assembled from the NVD JSON API; see also OSV entry.
bitmessage_link: Eval injection in constructObject (src/messagetypes/__init__.py) reachable by any sender because every node decodes every msg object; CVE-2021-26917 is a minor apinotifypath issue.

title: Security analysis: Bitmessage vulnerability assessment regarding quantum computing threats (PyBitmessage issue 2344)
note: Short issue text by an individual maintainer of forks (MiNode-Refined, PyBitRefined); weak as a paper but dated and technical, so kept as report.
bitmessage_link: Argues that secp256k1 static keys plus public storage of all ciphertext make Bitmessage a harvest-now-decrypt-later target; no forward secrecy, no post-quantum KEM.

title: Design and Analysis of an Improved BitMessage Anti-spam Mechanism
note: Only peer-reviewed analysis of the PoW admission rule; copy is the author-hosted PDF (Wayback copy of Telecom Paris page).
bitmessage_link: Analyses the proof-of-work formula that admits objects; shows legitimate senders and spammers pay the same price and proposes a decoupling that halves what a spammer gains.

title: Bitmessage Plus: A Blockchain-Based Communication Protocol With High Practicality
note: Direct successor proposal; the stealth-address step lets a recipient test an address tag instead of attempting full ECIES decryption, but scanning remains linear.
bitmessage_link: Redesign that replaces PoW by proof of space, replaces flood-and-trial-decrypt by stealth-address destinations, and stores messages on a chain; keeps the broadcast of every message.

title: Argumentation-Based Security Requirements Analysis: BitMessage Case Study
note: Paywalled (IEEE); metadata only. Software-engineering viewpoint, not a cryptographic analysis.
bitmessage_link: Applies a requirements-argumentation method (RISA) to Bitmessage to derive its security requirements and gaps.

title: Cryptoanalytic Code-Review of an encrypted P2P Message Service called "Bitmessage"
venue: Bachelor thesis, HTW Berlin (advisor D. Weber-Wulff), April 2014
note: Only hosted on ResearchGate (login or bot wall); not downloaded. Request the file from the author or the HTW thesis list.
bitmessage_link: Reads PyBitmessage 0.4.2 line by line: ECIES parameters, key derivation from addresses, PoW and the Bitcoin-derived pieces.

title: A branch hash function as a method of message synchronization in anonymous P2P conversations
venue: Int. J. Appl. Math. Comput. Sci. 26(2)
note: Gold OA. Most detailed academic discussion of Bitmessage streams, 48-hour retention and scalability among the sources found.
bitmessage_link: Proposes Aldeon, a group-conversation protocol that replaces Bitmessage flooding with tree synchronisation; its related-work survey compares Bitmessage, ShadowChat and Bleep and names trial decryption by every node as the main drawback.

title: Anonymity in Bitcoin and Bitmessage (bmd Go re-implementation and Shufflepuff)
venue: MS report, University of Texas at Austin
note: Repository returns 403 to scripted clients (bot wall), so not downloaded.
bitmessage_link: Describes bmd, a Go re-implementation of the Bitmessage protocol, its design and a performance analysis; the only measured cost study of a Bitmessage node found.

title: PyBit Forensic Investigation
venue: Chapter, A Practical Hands-on Approach to Database Forensics (Studies in Big Data 114), Springer
note: Paywalled (Springer).
bitmessage_link: Forensic examination of the PyBitmessage SQLite databases (messages, senders, recipients, pubkeys, inventory) to recover who talked to whom on a seized client.

title: Anonymous Stochastic Routing
note: Closest theory source on the cost of flooding for recipient anonymity.
bitmessage_link: Models recipient-anonymous routing and proves the anonymity-versus-delay trade-off; cites Bitmessage-style uniform flooding as the baseline that its routing policies beat.

title: EFPIX: An Encrypted Flood Protocol for Metadata-Resistant Communication
note: Single-author preprint; cites Bitmessage for identity management and compares features in a table.
bitmessage_link: A modern flood-relay design in Bitmessage style: PoW, dedup and aging against spam, per-correspondent aliases so recipients do not trial-decrypt everything.

title: Monero's Decentralized P2P Exchanges: Functionality, Adoption, and Privacy Risks
note: Evidence for a live Bitmessage derivative (SMSG). Authors read from the arXiv PDF title page.
bitmessage_link: Describes Particl SMSG, a Bitmessage-inspired flooding mixnet with 48-hour retention, as the order-book transport of BasicSwap and discusses its privacy risks.

title: SoK: Secure Messaging
bitmessage_link: Table III classes Bitmessage as a broadcast-based transport: high bandwidth, no asynchronicity, PoW or fees to limit spam; the standard systematisation entry for Bitmessage. Other slices hold three copies (secure-messaging, sok-secure-messaging, tr).

title: BIP 47: Reusable Payment Codes for Hierarchical Deterministic Wallets
bitmessage_link: Defines Bitmessage notification: a payment-code recipient derives a Bitmessage address from the code so the sender can post the code over Bitmessage instead of an on-chain notification; a use of Bitmessage as a recipient-hiding channel. Another copy exists as 2015-bip47-payment-codes.

title: bmd: Bitmessage full node written in Go (README)
note: Thin README; the design discussion is in the 2018 UT report. Repo last pushed 2017.
bitmessage_link: Go full node and client daemon split (bmd, bmclient) modelled on btcsuite; follows the original protocol and so inherits its flooding and trial decryption.

title: MiNode: Python 3 implementation of the Bitmessage protocol (README)
note: Shows the usual rewrite pattern: keep the flooding layer, drop the client, add an anonymising transport.
bitmessage_link: Object-routing-only Bitmessage node in Python 3 with I2P (SAM v3) transport; archived 2020, later forked as MiNode-Refined.

title: PyBitmessage-I2P: PyBitmessage fork that runs natively over I2P (README)
note: Answers the source-anonymity gap of Bitmessage by changing transport only.
bitmessage_link: A separate I2P-only Bitmessage network with BM+ addresses; hides node IPs through I2P while the application-layer flood is unchanged.

title: Ripple (bitmessage-rs): rewrite of Bitmessage in Rust on libp2p
note: README is a screenshot page with one sentence; no design document, so metadata only.
bitmessage_link: Rust rewrite on libp2p with its own network protocol, not compatible with PyBitmessage; GossipSub replaces raw inv/getdata flooding.

title: kashikoibumi/PyBitmessage: Python 3 and PyQt5 port of the reference client
note: Repository metadata only.
bitmessage_link: Python 3 port of the reference client; the official client was still Python 2 based at this date.

title: sergiorandria/bitmessage: Bitmessage client in Rust, all connections through Tor (arti)
note: Repository created 2026-08; metadata only.
bitmessage_link: Rust client that routes every connection through Tor using arti; again changes the transport, not the flood-and-decrypt core.

title: EIP-627: Whisper Specification
note: Created 2017-05-05. Another slice holds copies (2015-eip627-whisper, 2017-eip627-whisper); same URL.
bitmessage_link: Direct descendant: a gossip-flooded envelope (expiry, TTL, topic, data, PoW nonce) with symmetric or asymmetric encryption; a Bloom filter over topics lets a peer ask for a subset instead of everything, trading receiver privacy for bandwidth.

title: Status 3/WHISPER-USAGE (v0.3)
note: Year approximate: spec numbered 3 in the Status stable set, v0.3.
bitmessage_link: How Status uses Whisper: topic derivation, partitioned public topics, per-chat symmetric keys, PoW and Bloom-filter settings; shows the practical receiver-privacy cost (nodes learn topic interest).

title: Status 4/WHISPER-MAILSERVER
note: Year approximate.
bitmessage_link: Mail servers that store Whisper envelopes for offline devices and replay them on request; the usual fix for the two-day expiry of flooded messages, at the cost of a trusted store that learns topics and request times.

title: Status 5/SECURE-TRANSPORT (v0.3)
note: Year approximate; bundle rotation and one-to-one sessions described.
bitmessage_link: X3DH-style pre-key bundles and a double ratchet over Whisper; adds the forward secrecy that Bitmessage lacks.

title: Status 10/WAKU-USAGE (v0.1)
note: Year approximate.
bitmessage_link: Move of Status from Whisper to Waku: same topic model, mailserver replaced by store protocol.

title: A Secure Mobile Messenger Based on Ethereum Whisper
note: Korean-language journal; access closed; third author surname only, from Crossref.
bitmessage_link: Mobile messenger built on Whisper; an application of the Bitmessage-style flooding layer on a blockchain network.

title: An approach of covert communication based on the Ethereum whisper protocol in blockchain
note: Publisher PDF returned 403 for scripted access; metadata only. Third author surname only, from Crossref.
bitmessage_link: Uses Whisper envelopes as a covert channel; indicates that flooded, topic-tagged, short-lived messages are hard to attribute.

title: A Decentralized Application for Secure Messaging in a Trustless Environment
note: Closed access; author list from OpenAlex (may be partial).
bitmessage_link: dApp messenger over Ethereum with Whisper transport.

title: Postal Services over Swarm (pss) README
note: Prefix length is the receiver-privacy knob: longer prefix means smaller anonymity set and less decryption work.
bitmessage_link: Messages routed towards a recipient overlay address with a prefix of chosen length; the neighbourhood, not the whole network, trial-decrypts. Successor to Whisper for Swarm.

title: The Book of Swarm: Storage and Communication Infrastructure for a Self-Sovereign Digital Society
note: Chapter on pss states it is Whisper-derived. Copy fetched is the later edition; first edition 2021.
bitmessage_link: Section 4.4 defines Trojan chunks: messages disguised as content-addressed chunks with mined nonces so that they land in the recipient neighbourhood; recipient trial-decrypts only chunks it stores. Direct answer to Bitmessage cost without full flooding.

title: Swarm: Storage and Communication Infrastructure for a Self-Sovereign Digital Society (whitepaper v1.0)
note: The URL was historically a 2016 paper; the file fetched is v1.0 of June 2021.
bitmessage_link: Network-layer description (forwarding Kademlia, privacy and caching) underlying pss; shorter than the book.

title: 6/WAKU1 (Waku v1, Whisper-derived)
note: Living spec; year approximate (2019 first version). Maintainer emails removed from saved text.
bitmessage_link: Whisper with PoW, Bloom-filter topic interest, light nodes and mailserver support kept; the immediate Whisper descendant and thus a Bitmessage cousin.

title: 8/WAKU-MAIL (Waku mailserver)
note: Living spec; year approximate.
bitmessage_link: Store-and-forward server protocol for flooded envelopes.

title: 10/WAKU2 (Waku v2 overview)
note: Living spec; year approximate.
bitmessage_link: Defines the Waku v2 protocol family on libp2p: relay, filter, store, lightpush, discovery; routing by pubsub topic and content topic instead of flooding a single namespace.

title: 11/WAKU2-RELAY
note: Living spec; year approximate.
bitmessage_link: GossipSub-based relay over shard-sized pubsub topics; the Waku replacement for whole-network Whisper flooding; receiver privacy rests on subscribing to shards, not on ambiguity.

title: 14/WAKU2-MESSAGE
note: Living spec; year approximate.
bitmessage_link: Message envelope: payload, content topic, timestamp, optional ephemeral flag and RLN proof; replaces Whisper PoW envelope field.

title: 12/WAKU2-FILTER
note: Living spec; year approximate.
bitmessage_link: Light-client subscription: a full node forwards only messages for named content topics; the node learns the client interests, the opposite of Bitmessage ambiguity.

title: 13/WAKU2-STORE
note: Living spec; year approximate.
bitmessage_link: Historical-message query by content topic and time range from store nodes; the store learns what a client asks for.

title: 19/WAKU2-LIGHTPUSH
note: Living spec; year approximate.
bitmessage_link: Resource-restricted publishers hand a message to a service node for relay; moves publishing trust to the service node and exposes the publisher IP to it.

title: 17/WAKU2-RLN-RELAY
note: Companion paper is catalogued as 2022-taheri-waku-rln-relay. Living spec; year approximate.
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage PoW admission with rate-limiting nullifiers: a zero-knowledge membership proof per epoch, slashing double signalling; anonymous anti-spam without hash work.

title: 26/WAKU2-PAYLOAD
note: Living spec; year approximate.
bitmessage_link: Payload encryption: symmetric or ECIES with signature options carried over from Whisper; noted for what is hidden (content, optionally sender) and what is not (content topic).

title: 53/WAKU2-X3DH
note: Living spec; year approximate.
bitmessage_link: X3DH key agreement for Waku one-to-one sessions; gives forward secrecy with pre-key bundles, absent in Bitmessage.

title: NOISE-X3DH-DOUBLE-RATCHET
note: Living spec; year approximate.
bitmessage_link: Noise-based session establishment plus double ratchet for Waku chat; the post-compromise security layer missing from Bitmessage.

title: 32/RLN-V1 (Rate Limit Nullifier)
note: Living spec; year approximate.
bitmessage_link: Rate-limiting nullifier construction with Shamir secret sharing in a Merkle membership proof; the anonymous-credential rate limiting used instead of PoW.

title: RLN-V2 (Rate Limit Nullifier V2)
note: Living spec; year approximate.
bitmessage_link: RLN with a per-epoch message budget instead of one message per epoch.

title: GOSSIPSUB-TOR-PUSH
note: Living spec; year approximate.
bitmessage_link: Publishes the first hop of a message through Tor to hide the origin IP from relay peers; a source-anonymity patch for gossip networks.

title: DANDELION (Waku v2 Dandelion)
note: Living spec; year approximate; sibling slices hold copies (2025-waku-dandelion-spec).
bitmessage_link: Stem-and-fluff propagation for Waku relay to hide the originating node; the source-anonymity technique Bitmessage never used.

title: LIBP2P-MIX (mix protocol for libp2p)
note: Living spec, large; also relevant to mixnet slices.
bitmessage_link: Sphinx-based mix layer for libp2p and Waku with cover traffic and DoS protection; replaces flooding by routed mix paths for sender anonymity.

title: RLN-STEALTH-COMMITMENTS
note: Living spec; year approximate.
bitmessage_link: Stealth-address-like commitments so RLN membership registrations are unlinkable to the registrant.

title: ADVERSARIAL-MODELS: Waku v2 adversarial models and attack-based threat list
note: Living spec; year approximate.
bitmessage_link: Threat list for Waku relay, filter, store and lightpush: sybil, eclipse, DoS, deanonymisation by the filter/store node.

title: WAKU-RLN-RELAY: Privacy-Preserving Peer-to-Peer Economic Spam Protection
bitmessage_link: Paper form of the RLN-based replacement for Bitmessage proof-of-work admission; economic rather than computational spam cost, with membership anonymity.

title: Waku: A Family of Modular P2P Protocols For Secure & Censorship-Resistant Communication
bitmessage_link: Overview paper of the Waku family, successor to Whisper which was itself the Bitmessage-style flooding layer of Ethereum.

title: Privacy-Preserving Spam-Protected Gossip-Based Routing
bitmessage_link: Spam-protected gossip routing through RLN; the academic counterpart of replacing PoW admission by anonymous rate limits.

title: NIP-01: Basic protocol flow description
note: Living spec; year approximate (project start 2019-2020).
bitmessage_link: Events signed with the author key, relays that store and serve them by filter; defines the relay model every DM scheme runs on (relay sees pubkeys, tags and filters).

title: NIP-04: Encrypted Direct Message (deprecated)
note: Marked unrecommended in favour of NIP-17; year approximate. Practical attacks in Kimura et al. 2025.
bitmessage_link: Legacy DM: kind-4 event, ECDH shared secret with AES-256-CBC, sender and recipient pubkeys and timing visible to relays. Unlike Bitmessage it hides nothing about the pair.

title: NIP-13: Proof of Work
note: Living spec; year approximate.
bitmessage_link: Hashcash-style leading-zero-bits proof carried in an event nonce tag; relays may require it as an anti-spam admission, the Bitmessage mechanism in a relay setting.

title: NIP-44: Encrypted Payloads (versioned)
note: Audited by Cure53 per the spec text; year approximate.
bitmessage_link: ECDH + HKDF + ChaCha20 + HMAC with padding; fixes the malleability and length leak of NIP-04; still no forward secrecy.

title: NIP-59: Gift Wrap
note: Living spec; year approximate.
bitmessage_link: Rumor, seal, gift wrap: the author event is sealed to the recipient, then wrapped under a throw-away key with randomised timestamps; hides the sender from relays but the recipient pubkey tag stays visible unless the recipient authenticates to fetch.

title: NIP-17: Private Direct Messages
note: Living spec; year approximate (merged around 2024).
bitmessage_link: Current DM scheme: NIP-44 encryption inside NIP-59 gift wraps, delivered to the relays listed in the recipient relay list; relay learns the recipient but not the sender. Receiver privacy is via relay choice, not ambiguity.

title: Not in The Prophecies: Practical Attacks on Nostr
note: IEEE paywall; no open copy found (checked OpenAlex). Metadata only.
bitmessage_link: Practical attacks on the Nostr DM and event-signing layers (including NIP-04 weaknesses); the only academic attack paper on Nostr private messaging located.

title: An Empirical Analysis of the Nostr Social Network: Decentralization, Availability, and Replication Overhead
note: Not about DMs specifically.
bitmessage_link: Measures relay availability, concentration and replication overhead; context for the cost and reliability of relay-based delivery that NIP-17 inherits.

title: bitchat Protocol Whitepaper (version 2.0, July 2026)
note: Version 2.0 dated 2026-07-06; first release 2025. Author attribution to the project, not a named person.
bitmessage_link: BLE mesh with controlled flood, TTL, dedup and jitter, Noise-encrypted private messages, Nostr bridge; states that unlinkable presence is not provided and packet length is observable. A flood-based relative of Bitmessage at the radio layer.

title: Source-Based Routing for BitChat Packets (v2)
note: Project doc; undated beyond repository history.
bitmessage_link: Replaces flooding with explicit source routes for known peers to cut radio load.

title: Metadata Analysis and Forensic Resilience Evaluation of Decentralized Messaging Applications Using NIST SP 800-86
note: Diamond OA. Small experiment on one rooted phone.
bitmessage_link: Forensic recovery experiment on Session and BitChat: 47 message records recovered for Session, 12 BLE hop events for BitChat; evidence of what local metadata a flooding mesh leaves.

title: Early Review of The BitChat Protocol
note: IEEE paywall; metadata only. Not read.
bitmessage_link: Protocol review of BitChat.

title: Mesh Messaging in Large-scale Protests: Breaking Bridgefy
note: ePrint copy.
bitmessage_link: Attacks on the Bluetooth-mesh messenger Bridgefy: deanonymisation of senders and recipients, content recovery and message forging; the standard negative result for mesh messengers.

title: Breaking Bridgefy, again: Adopting libsignal is not enough
bitmessage_link: Follow-up attacks on the Bluetooth-mesh messenger after it adopted libsignal; shows that a ratcheting layer does not repair flood-mesh metadata leaks.

title: Strong Anonymity for Mesh Messaging
bitmessage_link: Proposes mesh messaging with anonymity against passive global adversaries, the design target that BLE-flood messengers such as bitchat do not reach.

title: ASMesh: Anonymous and Secure Messaging in Mesh Networks Using Stronger, Anonymous Double Ratchet
note: Gold OA at ACM but scripted download returned 403; metadata only. Check IACR ePrint for a copy.
bitmessage_link: Anonymous double ratchet for mesh networks with broadcast delivery, giving post-compromise security while recipients identify their messages without a stable identifier.

title: Amigo: Secure Group Mesh Messaging in Realistic Protest Settings
note: Scripted ACM download returned 403; metadata only.
bitmessage_link: Group messaging for mesh networks under protest conditions, with membership, forward secrecy and delivery under partial connectivity.

title: FoSAM: Forward Secret Messaging in Ad-Hoc Networks
note: Preprint.
bitmessage_link: Forward-secret messaging for ad-hoc and mesh networks without servers; targets the missing key-evolution of flood-based messengers.

title: Zcash Protocol Specification (living document, version fetched 2026-09-30)
note: Living spec; this copy is version v2026.7.0-236 [NU6.2]. Another slice holds the same file as 2016-zcash-protocol-spec.pdf (identical sha256).
bitmessage_link: Defines note encryption and the incoming-viewing-key trial decryption by which a wallet finds its notes among all shielded outputs; the receiver-side scan that mirrors Bitmessage trial decryption on a blockchain.

title: ZIP 307: Light Client Protocol for Payment Detection
note: Created 2018-09-17, status Draft; original author George Tankersley, owners Grigg and Hopwood. Other slices hold copies (2018-zcash-zip307, 2020-zip307-light-client).
bitmessage_link: Compact blocks give light clients the first bytes of each output ciphertext so they can trial-decrypt cheaply; states bandwidth 116 bytes per output and the trade-off of server-side filtering.

title: Penumbra protocol: Fuzzy Message Detection (S-FMD) chapters and note ciphertexts
note: Seven mdBook pages concatenated. Other slices hold 2022-penumbra-fmd and 2022-penumbra-fmd-spec variants.
bitmessage_link: Detection keys let an untrusted server pre-filter outputs with a tunable false-positive rate, removing most of the full-chain trial decryption; the production design of what Beck et al. proposed.

title: Fuzzy Message Detection
bitmessage_link: The CCS 2021 construction that lets a server filter messages for a client with a chosen false-positive rate; replaces Bitmessage download-everything with a tunable ambiguity set.

title: The Effect of False Positives: Why Fuzzy Message Detection Leads to Fuzzy Privacy Guarantees?
bitmessage_link: Shows that the false-positive rate that gives FMD its ambiguity is hard to choose; places a limit on how much hiding a detection key buys.

title: Oblivious Message Retrieval
bitmessage_link: Server retrieves the messages for a client without learning which; the cryptographic upper bound on the Bitmessage flood-and-scan idea, at high server compute cost.

title: Effective Anonymous Messaging: the Role of Altruism
note: Preprint.
bitmessage_link: Game-theoretic model of FMD: users choose how much cover traffic to download; selfish users do not, so anonymity needs altruists; the incentive version of the Bitmessage bandwidth cost.

title: Anonymity Analysis of the Umbra Stealth Address Scheme on Ethereum
note: Preprint; discusses linear scanning cost and signalling as remedies.
bitmessage_link: Heuristics identify the real recipient for about half of Umbra stealth payments; measured anonymity of a deployed receiver-scanning scheme (recipient scans announcements by trial).

title: Wesh Protocol (Berty): protocol documentation
note: Page text only; undated, year approximate (Wesh named 2021).
bitmessage_link: Offline-first protocol with group logs synchronised over BLE, mDNS and IPFS/libp2p pubsub; messages travel by group topic rather than recipient flooding.

title: Quiet: encrypted p2p team chat over Tor (README)
note: README only; undated, year approximate.
bitmessage_link: Closed communities sync over Tor onion services with OrbitDB; no global flood, so no ambiguity set but the community graph is hidden from outsiders; README states it is unaudited.
